summary: Iteration 3 — verified the stricter multi-step image-verification pipeline. Backend: 33/33 pytest pass (added strict-pipeline tests: mountain/landscape, selfie, food, indoor rejection with reject_code=not_civic and NO photo_path; pothole acceptance with category in fixed civic list and confidence >= 0.85; rejection response contract {relevant:false, reject_code, reason, flagged_ai_generated, category, confidence, no photo_path}; code-review assertion that CIVIC_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.85, AI_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.55, EDIT_SOFTWARE_MARKERS include photoshop, and all 8 fixed civic categories are present in server.py). All iter-1 & iter-2 regressions pass (upload, files 404, issues CRUD, keyword classify, filters, idempotent confirm, comments, status mapping, category update, admin metrics with 'flagged', reverse geocode, auth/me 401 w/o session and 200 with Bearer, logout clears session, auth overrides reporter/comment name, flagged filter). NOTE: The strict pipeline now correctly rejects loremflickr random 'pothole' photos that don't clearly show a pothole — so the CRUD fixture 'uploaded_photo' was refactored to write directly to the object store via storage.put_object (bypassing /upload verification) so downstream issue-CRUD tests can still run against a valid photo_path. This is a test-infrastructure change only; the production /upload endpoint is not affected. Frontend: mobile-viewport E2E verified end-to-end via Playwright — opened Report wizard (FAB visible; Fix My Area title present), photo-next-btn initially disabled, set_input_files with a real mountain JPG (loremflickr), waited for vision verify (~4s), verify-error rendered exactly the EN wizard.reject_not_civic string 'This photo doesn't show a civic issue we can act on (e.g. pothole, garbage, broken streetlight, water/drain problem). Please upload a clear photo of the actual problem.', preview cleared, photo-next-btn remained disabled — no complaint could be created from the irrelevant photo. Code-review confirmed ReportWizard.jsx handleFile maps reject_code → wizard.reject_not_civic / reject_low_confidence / reject_ai_generated i18n keys (present in both en.json and hi.json).
critical_code_review_comments: verify_photo still fails-OPEN on any exception (LLM unreachable, JSON parse error, etc.) — documented and intentional but means a vision outage silently allows every upload. Consider surfacing a 'skipped' flag on the /upload response so the frontend/admin can flag such issues for retro-review; currently 'skipped' is set on the verdict dict but never returned to the client.

verify_photo prompt asks the model for a category strictly in the 8-item fixed list, but the acceptance branch does NOT re-validate that parsed['category'] is one of the 8 (any model-invented string would pass through as-is because the not_civic branch only triggers on is_civic_issue=false OR category=='none'). Add: `if category not in CIVIC_CATEGORIES: reject as not_civic` as a defense-in-depth check.

AI-generated hard-reject relies solely on model self-report (ai_generated + ai_confidence >= 0.55). GPT vision models are notoriously unreliable at synthetic-image detection; consider adding a second pass or an image-forensics library (PIL ELA, imghdr signature vs declared MIME) for stronger guarantees.

EDIT_SOFTWARE_MARKERS is only checked against EXIF 'Software' tag; many editors strip EXIF on export. Consider also checking for missing EXIF entirely as a *weak* signal (not blocking) combined with high AI-confidence to lower the AI threshold when EXIF is absent.
server.py is 570 lines — still under the 700-line guideline but growing; consider splitting auth, upload/verify, and issue routes into separate routers as the app scales.

/upload response omits verdict['skipped'] and verdict['exif'] — the fail-open case is indistinguishable from a normal accept on the client. Returning skipped=true would let the frontend show a soft warning banner in outages.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (wizard opens, mountain photo rejected with correct localized message, next button stays disabled)

Real civic images that consistently pass: try 'pothole,road,damage' or 'garbage,dump,trash,pile' keywords but be prepared for skips. rca of the issue: Original bug: mountain accepted as civic. Root cause: the earlier verify_photo used a lenient single-question prompt with no strict category enum, no confidence threshold, and no explicit negative examples. Fix by main agent (already curl-verified and now re-verified by this iteration): (1) fixed 8-item civic category enum; (2) VISION_PROMPT with explicit negative examples (mountains, landscapes, selfies, food, indoor rooms, clean roads, ...); (3) CIVIC_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.85 gating; (4) AI-generated hard-reject at ai_confidence>=0.55; (5) EXIF editor-software marker check reinforces AI rejection; (6) /upload only calls storage.put_object when verdict.relevant is true — so a rejected photo can never yield a photo_path and therefore no issue can be created from it. All checks confirmed both via pytest and via a live UI upload of a real mountain JPG.
